restated_task: Implement the is_balanced(s) function in brackets/core.py so that it returns True when the three bracket types (), [], {} in the string s are correctly matched and nested, ignoring non-bracket characters. The empty string is balanced. The function must return a bool and raise TypeError if s is not a string. The existing is_bracket helper and the test suite must not be modified.

interface_contract.name: is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if the string s contains correctly matched and nested brackets of types (), [], {}. Non-bracket characters are ignored. The empty string is considered balanced. Returns False otherwise.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when s is not a string.

interface_contract.name: is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if c is a single character string that is one of the six bracket characters '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}'. Returns False otherwise.

acceptance_criteria: 1. The empty string '', '()', '[]', '{}', '()[]{}', '([{}])' are all balanced (return True).
2. Nested mixed brackets with other characters are balanced: '(a[b]{c})', 'f(x[0], y[1])' return True.
4. Non-bracket characters are ignored (they do not affect balancing).
5. is_balanced returns a bool (True or False).
6. TypeError is raised when s is not a string.
out_of_scope: The is_bracket function must not be changed.
The test file tests/test_basic.py must not be changed.
The brackets/__init__.py file must not be changed.
No other files in the repository may be modified.
